title: Jamaican Oxtail Stew
subtitle: Slow-braised oxtail with butter beans and scotch bonnet
excerpt: Oxtail braised low and slow in a rich, spiced gravy with butter beans, scotch bonnet, and allspice until the meat slips off the bone. A weekend dish that fills the kitchen with the smell of the Caribbean.
sourceNotes: Jamaican home cooking and a cornerstone of the Caribbean Sunday table. Common across Jamaica and in Jamaican communities in the UK.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze in portions with the braising liquid. Reheat gently on the hob over a low heat, adding a splash of water if needed.
recipe.batchNotes: Oxtail improves with size. Double the batch in a larger pot; the cooking time remains the same.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: The stew is better the next day. Make a day ahead and refrigerate. The fat will solidify on top; lift it off before reheating.

content.text: Oxtail needs time and nothing else can substitute for it. Three hours at a low, steady simmer is the minimum for the collagen to break down into the silky, glossy gravy this dish is known for. Keep the scotch bonnet whole so the heat is present but not piercing.
Season the oxtail pieces all over with salt and black pepper. Heat the oil in the dutch oven over a high heat. Brown the oxtail in batches, 4 minutes per side, until deep brown. Set aside.
Lower the heat to medium. Add the onion to the pot and cook for 6 minutes until soft and golden. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute. Add the sugar and stir for 30 seconds.
Add the tomato puree and stir for 1 minute. Pour in the stock, soy sauce, and Worcestershire sauce. Stir well.

Return the oxtail to the pot. Add the scotch bonnet whole, spring onions, thyme, allspice berries, and bay leaves. The liquid should come about two-thirds of the way up the oxtail. Add water if needed.
Bring to a gentle simmer, cover tightly, and cook over a low heat for 2.5 to 3 hours, turning the oxtail halfway through. The meat should be very tender and falling from the bone.

Remove and discard the scotch bonnet, thyme sprigs, and bay leaves. Stir in the butter beans and simmer uncovered for 15 minutes until the gravy has thickened and the beans are heated through. Taste and adjust seasoning. Rest for 10 minutes before serving with rice.

items.symptom: The meat is still tough at 3 hours.
items.cause: The heat was too low or the pot was losing steam.
items.fix: The simmer should be a steady, low bubble throughout. Check the lid seal and raise the heat slightly. Add another 30 to 45 minutes if needed.

items.cause: The scotch bonnet split during cooking.
items.fix: Next time, leave the scotch bonnet completely whole and handle it gently. Remove it after 1 hour if you want less heat.

items.cause: The lid was kept on throughout and liquid did not reduce.
items.fix: Simmer uncovered for 20 to 30 minutes after the meat is tender to reduce the gravy to the right consistency.
